analysis.title: US Economic Notes: What you need to know for the week ahead
key_insights: DB expects September headline CPI at +0.57% m/m (vs +0.40% previous), boosted by a 9.6% rise in seasonally adjusted motor fuel prices, well above core at +0.16% (vs +0.29%).
If DB forecasts hit, headline CPI y/y rises about 24bps to 3.64% while core CPI y/y slips a couple of basis points from 2.45% to 2.39%.
Core goods prices are forecast unchanged. DB is watching for declines in used car prices and medical care commodities, offset by strength in recreation and information technology commodities.
On services, last month's spike in wireless services prices should roll off, while higher jet fuel prices should support airfares.
Thursday's PPI and Friday's import prices will show the read-through to core PCE. DB forecasts a 0.21% rise in August core PCE (vs +0.25% in August), keeping the y/y rate roughly steady at 3.0%.

PPI and import prices are the last inflation datapoints Fed officials will have before the October 28 FOMC. If they land near DB forecasts, the Fed can hold in October and wait for more information before December.

Recent Fedspeak from Vice Chair Jefferson, NY Fed President Williams and Governor Waller says more tightening is likely needed but timing is flexible and not urgent. DB reads this as a strong base case of skipping October and hiking again in December.
Chair Warsh's Thursday fireside chat with IMF MD Georgieva is the last Fed speaker event before the blackout and the last and clearest chance to change the message.
At the September FOMC Warsh made a relatively hawkish case: policy is accommodative and the first move was to 'remove a dose of accommodation'.

September FOMC minutes showed varied motives for hiking: many cited risk management or insurance, a number cited higher inflation in their modal outlooks, some cited unanchoring of inflation expectations, and a couple cited second-round effects from supply shocks or higher neutral rate estimates.
Several officials viewed the policy rate as not restrictive or only mildly restrictive, a view Warsh said had become broadly accepted in the Committee.
Barring a meaningful and broad-based upside inflation miss this week, DB expects the Fed to hold in October, and also to monitor financial conditions after sharp moves in global interest rates.

risk_factors: A meaningful and broad-based upside miss in this week's CPI and PPI inflation data could change the Fed's October hold.
Chair Warsh's Thursday fireside chat could change the Fed's message before the blackout.
Sharp moves in global interest rates may tighten financial conditions further.
